summary: Initial integration discovery for Cascade Systems evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Focus on SDK support (python/js), LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, gateway/proxy integration, rate limits/quotas, observability hooks, and security (VPC, SOC2, KMS). Customer leans towards Dedicated for predictable latency but needs clarity on deployment path and cost tradeoffs.
topics: security: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, private VPC
transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Ava, AE on this account, with Ethan from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Priya (Cascade): Good thanks. We have about 45 minutes. Priya Rao here, CTO. Marcus and Sofia are with me.
[00:12] Marcus (Cascade): Hi all.
[00:14] Ethan (Redwood): Great. Quick agenda — understand your current stack, integration constraints, latency SLOs, and security requirements; then talk through SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex support, and how the gateway/proxy would sit in front of Redwood.
[00:25] Priya: Sounds good. High level — we're building a customer support summarization + routing service. We care a lot about 95th percentile latency under load, and cost. We currently run models in-house on k8s with a custom gateway, but we're hitting ops limits.
[00:38] Sofia: Our infra is AWS, VPCs, private subnets, we use Cognito for SSO but planning to move to SAML soon. We also have strict data retention and audit log needs.
[00:47] Ava: Understood. Do you have a preference Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private at this stage?
[00:53] Priya: Prefer Dedicated if it gives predictable latency and isolation. But we want to understand migration lift and whether hosted can meet our P95 target during spikes.
[01:05] Ethan: For Dedicated we provide reserved GPU pools with autoscaling and burst capacity. Important note — you can pin model versions and set routing policies. For Hosted you'd get fast onboarding but less isolation. For Private we'd provide a customer-managed control plane — more lift but meets the strictest compliance.
[01:23] Marcus: Can you walk through SDKs? Our stack uses Python and Node, and we're using LangChain in some services and LlamaIndex in another.
[01:31] Ethan: Sure. We have first-class SDKs for Python and JS with examples. For LangChain we maintain official adapters and a sample repo; same with LlamaIndex, though community forks exist and sometimes names get mangled in transcription, e.g., people say Llama-index or Llama idx, but we've got a stable integration. The LangChain adapter wraps Redwood routes and handles streaming tokens, function calling, and structured output.
[01:55] Priya: Do you support streaming with LangChain?
[01:57] Ethan: Yes — streaming is supported via our SDK and can be plumbed into LangChain callbacks. For large responses we do incremental tokens and you can subscribe to partial responses.
[02:08] Sofia: On our side we have an internal gateway/proxy (kong + envoy) that terminates TLS and enforces rate limits. How does Redwood fit behind a gateway? We prefer not to expose backend keys.
[02:19] Ava: Most customers front Redwood with their gateway — they either use IP allowlists + mTLS or a short-lived token exchange. For Dedicated we can set up private peering and internal endpoints. For Hosted there's an option to use a customer-side proxy that performs key exchange and token minting.
[02:36] Marcus: What about throttling? We need rate limits per-tenant and burst behavior.
[02:40] Ethan: We have per-api-key quotas and rate limits. For Dedicated you also get configurable policies at the cluster/route level and burst windows. Our console shows per-route token usage and enforcement. Caveat: if you're doing extreme burst, consider enabling burst capacity or a degrade policy to a smaller model to preserve availability.
[03:03] Priya: Observability is critical — we need traces correlated with our request IDs, token-level cost breakdown, and per-route latency histograms.
[03:11] Ethan: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, and tracing hooks. We support passing an x-request-id that gets surfaced in logs; we also have tracing integrations and can forward logs to your Splunk/Datadog.
[03:24] Sofia: Do you emit audit logs for every request? We're subject to internal audits.
[03:28] Ava: Yes — Dedicated and Private deployments include detailed audit logs, retention configurable as an add-on. Hosted includes audit logs but retention tiers differ. We'll share the SOC2 / audit pack.
[03:39] Marcus: Encryption? KMS? HSM?
[03:41] Ethan: We integrate with customer KMS for Private and Dedicated via CMKs and offer HSM-backed key options for high-security customers. For Hosted we manage keys but offer dedicated customer KMS in enterprise plans.
[03:55] Priya: For the LangChain integration, we need an example pipeline that uses our prompt templates, chat layering, and embeddings for reranking. Can you run a bench with our templates?
[04:05] Ava: Yes — propose a benchmark: we'll request a small pilot where Marcus provides sample prompts and a dataset. We'll run a latency+throughput test against your SLAs and share results.
[04:15] Marcus: Good. Also — we use LlamaIndex to build an index over support docs; does Redwood provide embeddings compatible with existing embedding vectors so we don't need to reindex?
[04:26] Ethan: We support a set of embedding models and can do vector versioning; however embedding formats and vector normalization vary, so typically customers reindex for optimal results. We can export embeddings to your S3 or provide a migration plan.
[04:40] Sofia: About SDK security — do the SDKs support token rotations and short-lived tokens?
[04:45] Ethan: Yes, SDK supports short-lived credentials and refresh flows. For Private/Dedicated you can plug into your identity provider for token issuance.
[04:54] Priya: Cost discussion — how do we estimate per-token cost and effect of batching/kv cache?
[04:59] Ava: Redwood Optimize recommends batching and caching settings. KV caching reduces repeated prefix cost heavily for chat scenarios. In Dedicated you can configure batching window vs latency SLO — our optimizer will suggest a profile. We'll send a cost model example.
[05:12] Marcus: Any gotchas with our gateway? We do header rewriting and some payload size limits.
[05:18] Ethan: Header rewriting is common; ensure x-request-id and any tracing headers pass through. Payload size limits — check max token size for the model family; we can support extended sequences on certain model variants but there may be cost/latency tradeoffs.
[05:33] Priya: Compliance — we need SOC2 + SSO (SAML) + audit logs and to know where data resides. Also request a copy of your data processing addendum.
[05:42] Ava: We'll share SOC2, DPA, and a data residency doc. For Dedicated/Private you can keep data in your VPC or region; Hosted gives region selection but logs may be aggregated unless configured otherwise.
[05:55] Marcus: One technical deep-dive question — how do you handle KV cache and prompt prefix caching with multiple instances to avoid cold-start latency?
[06:03] Ethan: Our runtime has distributed KV cache with sticky routing for sessions; we also support a shared cache layer so repeated prefixes hit the cache. There are some tradeoffs in Dedicated depending on cluster size — we'll surface best practices in the integration checklist.
[06:20] Priya: Ok let's talk timeline — we want a pilot in July if the benchmark looks good. Decision maker will be Priya + infra leads.
[06:28] Ava: Good. We'll follow up with pricing and a pilot scope.
[06:32] Sofia: If you could also include example rate-limit configs for per-tenant throttling that would help us map to our gateway.
[06:39] Ethan: Will do — sample configs for Kong/envoy + our policy.
[06:44] Priya: A couple of quick clarifications: do you support on-prem air-gapped deployment?
[06:48] Ava: Yes — Private on-prem is an option though it requires more ops and support. We have an air-gapped package and can talk through installation windows.
[06:57] Marcus: Competitors — we've looked at OpenAI for hosted, Anthropic for some models. Concern is vendor lock and cost.
[07:06] Ava: Understandable. For Dedicated we support open models too which reduces lock-in and gives cost control via quantization.
[07:15] Priya: Great. We're also interested in the observability hooks — can you push traces to our Datadog and provide a webhook on quality alerts?
[07:24] Ethan: Yes on Datadog. We also support webhook alerts for regression or quality alerts tied to prompt sets; Redwood Optimize can send alerts when evals degrade.
[07:34] Ava: Alright let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[07:37] Ava: 1) We'll send Dedicated pricing and SLA; 2) Ethan will prepare LangChain/LlamaIndex sample repo and sample benchmark plan; 3) Customer will share gateway config and sample prompts/dataset for the benchmark; 4) We'll schedule the benchmark week of 6/22.
[07:55] Priya: That works.
[07:58] Ava: Any final questions?
[08:00] Sofia: None from me.
[08:02] Marcus: All good.
[08:04] Ava: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links.
[08:08] Priya: Thanks, bye.
[08:10] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard words and product names, e.g., 'KV cash' instead of KV cache, 'Lang-Chain' variants. There was natural crosstalk and short interruptions.

References shared during call: "Dedicated_pricing_v1.pdf" (link sent via follow-up), "LangChain_sample_repo" (GitHub link to be shared), SOC2 pack (link), benchmark plan template (Google Sheet).

End of transcript.
